bug_description.normalized: The saved TopicTree fuzz witness is a byte stream that `makeChunked()` splits by one-byte chunk sizes. Early `S` chunks build a subscription tree with exact-child, `+`, and `#` nodes, and later non-empty `P` chunks publish attacker-controlled topics into that tree. In vulnerable `TopicTree::publish(Topic *, ...)`, the only capacity guard for `triggeredTopics[64]` is the worker-entry `if (numTriggeredTopics == 64) { drain(); }` at lines 124-126. The reproduced UBSan stack shows repeated recursion through line 146 before the crash at line 163, and the only source-level statements inside `publish()` that increase the shared `numTriggeredTopics` counter are the append assignments at lines 139 and 163. Because the current frame does not rerun the capacity check after recursive calls change that shared counter, recursive append(s) can raise `numTriggeredTopics` to 64 before the current exact-match append executes `triggeredTopics[numTriggeredTopics++] = iterator`, reproducing the `index 64 out of bounds for type 'uWS::Topic *[64]'` write at `src/TopicTree.h:163`.

source.code: stop = topic.find('/', start); std::string_view segment = topic.substr(start, stop - start);
source.description: First project-code statement on the witnessed path that consumes attacker-controlled input and materializes slash-delimited subscription segments. Those segments are then used to create the tree structure that the crashing publish later traverses.
source.value_from: `makeChunked()` reads the first size byte `0xe7`, yielding a 231-byte chunk whose payload is `id = 0`, `action = 'S'`, and a 226-byte topic string dominated by `+`, `/`, and `#`. `operator()` forwards that string into `TopicTree::subscribe()`, which begins parsing it here.

tainted_value_origin.description: For each emitted chunk longer than four bytes, the harness interprets bytes 0..3 as a subscriber id, byte 4 as an action, and bytes 5..end as `lastString`. On `S` chunks that string becomes the subscription topic, and on `P` chunks it becomes both the publish topic and the message payload.

root_cause.description: The only capacity check for the fixed `triggeredTopics[64]` array runs at recursive worker entry, before the frame's wildcard recursion. Vulnerable `publish()` never reruns `if (numTriggeredTopics == 64) { drain(); }` immediately before either append statement at lines 139 or 163.
root_cause.note: The staged patch deletes this worker-entry guard, reinserts the same `if (numTriggeredTopics == 64) { drain(); }` immediately before both append sites at lines 139 and 163, and rejects published `+` and `#` segments so wildcard recursion cannot keep growing the batch unchecked.

sink.description: Observed crash site. By the time this final exact-match append executes on the witnessed path, earlier recursive append(s) in the same publish operation have already advanced the shared counter to 64, so this statement computes subscript 64 on the 64-slot `triggeredTopics` array.
sink.note: Stage 01 reproduced `../src/TopicTree.h:163:13: runtime error: index 64 out of bounds for type 'uWS::Topic *[64]'`, and the saved stack shows repeated parent frames at line 146 before returning to this write.

parser_admitted.description: The witness's first decoded chunk has action `S`, so the staged input reaches project code by forwarding its topic string into `TopicTree::subscribe()`.

publish_invoked.description: The reproduced stack contains `fuzzing/TopicTree.cpp:68`, proving that a later non-empty `P` chunk reaches the publish arm used by the crash.

evidence_limitations: The saved UBSan stack proves the crash goes through `fuzzing/TopicTree.cpp:68` and repeated recursive `publish()` frames at line 146, but it does not identify which decoded `P` chunk among the witness's many non-empty `P` chunks is the final crashing publish.

The staged artifacts prove recursive `publish()` frames run before the line-163 crash, and source shows that only lines 139 and 163 increment `numTriggeredTopics`; they do not disambiguate which recursive append site performs the final pre-sink increment that brings the shared counter to 64.
Stage 02 did not rerun the fixed build, so `patch_resolves` is source-grounded from the staged diff rather than dynamically confirmed.

coarse_trace.summary: The witness starts with attacker-controlled `S` chunks whose topic strings are parsed into segments and inserted into `TopicTree`, creating both ordinary `children` edges and `+`/`#` wildcard pointers.

A later non-empty `P` chunk publishes another attacker-controlled topic into that wildcard-heavy tree. Recursive `publish()` follows `wildcardChild` branches before the current frame resumes its own exact-match path.

Because the only `numTriggeredTopics == 64` guard runs once at worker entry and is not repeated at the append sites, recursive append(s) can fill the shared 64-slot batch before a later exact-match append at line 163 writes out of bounds.

fine_trace.note: `makeChunked()` first consumes a one-byte chunk size, then within each emitted chunk bytes 0..3 are the subscriber id, byte 4 is the action, and bytes 5..end become `lastString`. That decoded field is later used as the subscription topic for `S` chunks and as the publish topic for `P` chunks.

fine_trace.code: stop = topic.find('/', start); std::string_view segment = topic.substr(start, stop - start);
fine_trace.note: Source. `subscribe()` begins consuming the attacker-controlled subscription topic by splitting it into slash-delimited segments. Those segment values drive every later node insertion and wildcard registration.

fine_trace.code: iterator->children.insert(lb, {std::string_view(newTopic->name, segment.length()), newTopic}); if (segment.length() == 1) { if (segment[0] == '+') { iterator->wildcardChild = newTopic; } if (segment[0] == '#') { iterator->terminatingWildcardChild = newTopic; } }
fine_trace.note: On previously unseen segments, `subscribe()` inserts a new `Topic` into `children`; single-character `+` and `#` segments additionally populate the fast `wildcardChild` and `terminatingWildcardChild` pointers. The witness's early `S` chunks therefore build the exact-child and wildcard structure that the later crashing publish traverses.

Later in the same witness, a non-empty `P` chunk routes another attacker-controlled string into `TopicTree::publish()`. The reproduced stack includes `fuzzing/TopicTree.cpp:68`, so the crashing path takes this non-empty publish arm rather than the empty-string fallback at line 71.
The public overload seeds the recursive worker from the root node with `start = 0`, `stop = 0`, and the attacker-controlled publish topic.

Root cause. This worker-entry guard runs before any wildcard recursion in the current frame. Vulnerable `publish()` does not rerun the same capacity check at the append sites after deeper recursive calls have changed the shared `numTriggeredTopics` counter.

fine_trace.code: stop = topic.find('/', start); std::string_view segment = topic.substr(start, stop - start);
fine_trace.note: The recursive worker consumes the published topic segment by segment. This parsed `segment` is then used for terminating-wildcard delivery, wildcard recursion, and exact child lookup.

fine_trace.code: if (iterator->wildcardChild) { publish(iterator->wildcardChild, stop + 1, stop, topic, message); }
fine_trace.note: If the current node has a `wildcardChild`, `publish()` recurses on the remaining topic suffix before the current frame continues its own exact-match path. Step 3 created these wildcard-child pointers from attacker-controlled `+` segments, and the saved UBSan stack shows repeated parent frames at line 146, so this recursive arm executes multiple times on the witnessed path.

fine_trace.code: if (!iterator->terminatingWildcardChild->triggered) { triggeredTopics[numTriggeredTopics++] = iterator->terminatingWildcardChild; iterator->terminatingWildcardChild->triggered = true; } if (!iterator->triggered) { triggeredTopics[numTriggeredTopics++] = iterator; iterator->triggered = true; }
fine_trace.note: Within the deeper recursive frames reached by step 8, these are the only source-level statements inside `publish()` that append into `triggeredTopics` and increment the shared `numTriggeredTopics` counter. One or more such recursive append(s) execute before the current frame resumes and raise the counter to 64; the saved artifacts do not disambiguate whether the final pre-sink increment is the terminating-wildcard append, a deeper exact-match append, or both.

fine_trace.code: std::map<std::string_view, Topic *>::iterator it = iterator->children.find(segment); if (it == iterator->children.end()) { return; } iterator = it->second;
fine_trace.note: After any deeper wildcard recursion returns, the current frame still follows its own exact child edge for the same `segment`. The crash at line 163 implies this lookup succeeds; otherwise control would return here before the sink.
The exact-match topic selected in step 10 is still untriggered in the crashing frame, so this frame will attempt one more append into the shared batch.

Sink. After step 9 has already raised the shared counter to 64 in deeper frames, the current frame's exact-match append at line 163 reuses that counter without any intervening append-site `drain()` check, so it computes `triggeredTopics[64]` and matches the reproduced UBSan report.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged diff removes the hoisted entry check, inserts the same `if (numTriggeredTopics == 64) { drain(); }` immediately before both append sites, and rejects `+` or `#` publish segments, so recursive growth is checked at the point of each append instead of only once at worker entry.

format.name: TopicTree byte-chunked fuzz witness
format.contract: Exact saved binary witness in `poc`. `makeChunked()` reads a one-byte chunk size (`0` means the rest of the buffer); each emitted chunk is then interpreted as `u32le subscriber_id | action | topic_bytes`. The file starts with size byte `0xe7`, yielding a 231-byte chunk with `id = 0`, `action = 'S'`, and a 226-byte topic dominated by `+`, `/`, and `#`. Later chunks include non-empty `P` actions; the reproduced stack proves one such chunk reaches `fuzzing/TopicTree.cpp:68` and reproduces the `index 64 out of bounds` write at `src/TopicTree.h:163`.
